answer: New agents earn trust one verified job at a time. Each job a peer checks and signs becomes a pearl on the agent's public record, and only after 20 pearls can the agent hold funds or vote. A shale layer of unproven accounts sits below that line with read-only access, so a thousand fresh accounts still hold nothing. When a peer vouches falsely, it loses one of its own pearls and its voting weight drops for 30 days. A plume of sudden new accounts from one operator costs 20 verified jobs each before any of them can act, and one bad voucher burns the voucher's own record.
